column1: # ZFS properties for opti's pool `red`, applied by apply-zfs-properties.sh from
# .github/workflows/opti-deploy.yml on every deploy. This file is the source of truth:
# a `zfs set` by hand on opti is reverted by the next deploy (for properties listed here).
# Format: dataset<TAB>property<TAB>value  (tabs or spaces; # starts a comment)
#   value `inherit` -> `zfs inherit` (removes a local setting). Deleting a line does NOT
#   undo it on the host; change the value to `inherit` (or `none` for quota/reservation),
#   deploy, then delete the line.
# Why each line (measured 2026-11-09, pool 3.62T at 76%, see README.md):
# red/media is Movies + Shows (Sonarr/Radarr write here over SMB from noblenumbat) and Assets
# (a copy of E:\Assets on ptm). 1.20T today. The quota caps it so the *arr stack can never
# fill the pool: at 1.5T media plus today's red/fs the pool tops out near 85%. The doctor
# warns at 90% of the quota (homelab-doctor.py QUOTA_WARN_PCT).
red/media
# Media is re-downloadable or mirrored, and *arr upgrades delete files, which snapshots would
# then hold for up to 12 months (monthly keep=12). NOTE: zfs-auto-snapshot also stops PRUNING
# a dataset once it is excluded, so snapshots taken before this was set never expire on their
# own and must be destroyed by hand (a separate, approved step).
red/media
# Guaranteed space for the app tier and homelab.db, so a full pool (a big copy into red/fs)
# cannot stop the vault, bots, notes, docker or the homelab-db from writing.
red/docker
red/docker-apps
red/opsdb
